content_markdown:
Disaster Stats
- **Internal displacements due to natural disasters:** {{hl}}5.4 million{{/hl}} displacements in India in 2024, the highest in {{hl}}12 years {{/hl}}([IDMC GRID 2025](https://www.internal-displacement.org/global-report/grid2025/))
- South Asia recorded over {{hl}}4.6 million{{/hl}} disaster displacements in 2025 out of {{hl}}29.9 million{{/hl}} globally ([IDMC GRID 2026](https://api.internal-displacement.org/sites/default/files/2026-05/IDMC-GRID-2026-Global-Report-on-Internal-Displacement.pdf))

• Droughts
- **Impact:** {{hl}}40%{{/hl}} land area and {{hl}}70 % of cultivable area{{/hl}} prone to droughts
- **Vulnerability:** Affect {{hl}}40% of population{{/hl}}
- {{hl}}60%{{/hl}} increase in droughts in last {{hl}}25 years{{/hl}}

• Earthquakes
- [[Data by NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf)]
- **Vulnerability:** ~{{hl}}59-60% of land{{/hl}}mass is prone to earthquakes ({{hl}}80% of population{{/hl}}) ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf))
    - **Unsustainable infra:** {{hl}}90%{{/hl}} casualties due to collapse of houses & structures

• Landslide
- {{hl}}12.6% of land area{{/hl}} is prone to landslides ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf) / [GSI](https://www.gsi.gov.in/)).

• Floods
- **Area:** {{hl}}12% of land area{{/hl}} (over {{hl}}40 million hectares{{/hl}}) prone to floods and river erosion ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf))
    - **Vulnerable sections:** Children and women, constitute {{hl}}85% of death{{/hl}}.
    - **Economic Losses:** average annual loss is estimated to be {{hl}}US$ 7.4 billion{{/hl}}

• Urban fire
- **Hotspots:** Maha & Guj accounts {{hl}}30%{{/hl}} of India’s fire accident deaths
- **Reasons:** {{hl}}60%{{/hl}} of Fire related deaths occur in Residential buildings.
- **Shortcomings:** {{hl}}65%{{/hl}} shortage of fire stations.
- **Impact:** {{hl}}4th biggest risk{{/hl}} to business continuity (India Risk Survey 2021)
- **Loss of life:** 35 people killed every day due to fire related incidents
- **Vulnerable section:** {{hl}}60%{{/hl}} of those killed are women

• Heatwave
- **Coverage:** {{hl}}90%{{/hl}} of India is in a “danger zone” from it ([PLOS Climate](https://journals.plos.org/climate/article?id=10.1371/journal.pclm.0000161)).
- **Financial loss:** ${{hl}}2,500 billion by 2030{{/hl}} (Globally)
- **Heat stress loss in India:** {{hl}}6%{{/hl}} of its working hours equivalent to 35 Million fulltime jobs ([ILO](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/@dgreports/@dcomm/@publ/documents/publication/wcms_711919.pdf))
- **Loss of life:** 155,937 heat-related deaths in India in 2021 (Global Burden of Disease study)

• Forest Fire
- **Causes:** Only {{hl}}4%{{/hl}} natural causes globally ([MoEFCC](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100))
- **Vulnerability:** >{{hl}}35% {{/hl}}(~{{hl}}36%{{/hl}}) of India's forest cover is prone to frequent forest fires ([FSI](https://fsi.nic.in/uploads/isfr2023/isfr_book_eng-vol-1_2023.pdf) / [ISFR 2023](https://fsi.nic.in/uploads/isfr2023/isfr_book_eng-vol-1_2023.pdf)).
    - **Carbon emission:** {{hl}}2.5 billion{{/hl}} to {{hl}}4.0 billion{{/hl}} tons annually ([IPCC](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/))
    - **Global:** Amazon forest **–** 8000 incidents in 2019

• Cyclones
- **Exposure:** India exposed to {{hl}}10%{{/hl}} of world’s tropical cyclones.
- **Extent:** ~{{hl}}75% {{/hl}}({{hl}}5,700 km{{/hl}}) of India's {{hl}}7,516.6 km{{/hl}} coastline (revised to {{hl}}11,098.8 km{{/hl}} in Dec 2024) prone to cyclones and tsunamis ([NDMA](https://nidm.gov.in/pdf/guidelines/floods.pdf)).
    - **Vulnerability:** {{hl}}8% of area{{/hl}} and 1/{{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} of Indians are vulnerable to cyclone

content_markdown:
GENERAL STATE OF ECONOMY (ECONOMIC SURVEY 2024-25)

• Global Growth
- **IMF Projections** -> {{hl}}3.2%{{/hl}} and {{hl}}3.3%{{/hl}} for 2024 and 2025, respectively ([IMF WEO](https://www.imf.org/en/Publications/WEO) / [Economic Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)).
    - Over the next {{hl}}5 years {{/hl}}→ average {{hl}}3.2%{{/hl}}.

• Resilient Domestic Economy
- **GDP Growth:** Real GDP grew by {{hl}}6.5%{{/hl}} in FY25 ({{hl}}6.7%{{/hl}} in Q1, {{hl}}5.4%{{/hl}} in Q2 FY25) and is estimated to grow by {{hl}}7.4%{{/hl}} in FY26 (FAE), with FY27 projected at {{hl}}6.8–7.2% {{/hl}}([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **GVA Growth:** Real Gross Value Added (GVA) is estimated to grow by {{hl}}7.3%{{/hl}} in FY26 (FAE), up from {{hl}}6.4%{{/hl}} in FY25 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **Primary Sector:** Agricultural growth rebounded to {{hl}}3.8%{{/hl}} in FY25 ({{hl}}4.4%{{/hl}} 5-year average; {{hl}}3.5%{{/hl}} in Q2 FY26) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **Secondary Sector:** Industry GVA grew by {{hl}}7.0%{{/hl}} in H1 FY26 (Manufacturing GVA grew {{hl}}7.72%{{/hl}} in Q1 and {{hl}}9.13%{{/hl}} in Q2 FY26), up from {{hl}}6.2%{{/hl}} in FY25 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
- **Tertiary Sector:** Services GVA is estimated to grow by {{hl}}9.1%{{/hl}} in FY26 ({{hl}}9.3%{{/hl}} in H1 FY26; {{hl}}56.4%{{/hl}} share in GVA), up from {{hl}}7.2%{{/hl}} in FY25 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).

subject: AGRICULTURE
content_markdown:
PRIMARY SECTOR

• Agriculture
• Eco Parameters
- **Share in GDP:** ~{{hl}}16% of GDP{{/hl}} ({{hl}}17.7%{{/hl}} of GVA) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **Growth Rate (Recent):** Agricultural growth rebounded from {{hl}}1.4%{{/hl}} in 2023-24 to {{hl}}3.8%{{/hl}} in 2024-25, and registered {{hl}}3.5%{{/hl}} in Q2 FY26 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **Growth Rate (Cumulative):** {{hl}}4.4%{{/hl}} average annual growth over the past {{hl}}5 years{{/hl}}, and {{hl}}4.45%{{/hl}} decadal growth during FY16 to FY25 (highest across decades) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
    - **Agri income:** ↑ {{hl}}5.23%{{/hl}} annually over the past decade.
- **People Employed:** employs ~{{hl}}46.1%{{/hl}} of the workforce ([PLFS 2023-24](https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/Press_note_AR_PLFS_2023_24_22092024.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
    - **Agri market:** &rupee;{{hl}}38 lakh crore by 2030{{/hl}}.
    - **India is 1st in:** Pulses, Milk
    - **India is 2nd in:** Rice, Wheat, Fruits & Vegetation, arable land.

• Land
• Area under Cultivation
- {{hl}}51% of total land{{/hl}} area is under cultivation.
- About {{hl}}60%{{/hl}} of India’s total land area is classified as agricultural land. [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]
• Small & Marginal farmers
- {{hl}}89.4% {{/hl}}(<2 hectares) [[Economic Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]
- Cultivate nearly {{hl}}45%{{/hl}} of net sown area ([Agri Census 2015-16](https://agcensus.da.gov.in/)).

• Seed
- **Saved Seeds** ↠ {{hl}}85%{{/hl}}
- **Seed Replacement Rate:** {{hl}}15 – 20%{{/hl}}; it’s {{hl}}100%{{/hl}} for hybrid seeds.
- **Production:** Private firms -> {{hl}}71%{{/hl}} of seed production ([ICAR](https://icar.org.in/))
- **Role of Seeds:** Impacts {{hl}}25%{{/hl}} of productivity

• Irrigation
- **Rainfed Agriculture:** {{hl}}50% of total{{/hl}}
- **Role of Irrigation:** {{hl}}70% of total{{/hl}} input cost
- **Irrigation coverage:** ↑ from {{hl}}49.3%{{/hl}} to {{hl}}55%{{/hl}} of gross cropped area b/w FY16 and FY21 [[Eco Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]

• Credit
- **Informal Sector:** around {{hl}}40%{{/hl}}
- **Debt:** More than {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} farmers under debt
- **BPL:** {{hl}}22% of farmers{{/hl}} are BPL
- **Corporate Investment** ↠ < {{hl}}2%{{/hl}}
- **Kisan Credit Card scheme:** {{hl}}7.72–7.75 crore{{/hl}} operational accounts ( ₹10+ lakh crore in KCC credit; total ground-level agricultural credit reached {{hl}}₹28.67 lakh crore in FY25{{/hl}}) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).

• Pesticides
- {{hl}}4th largest producer{{/hl}} of pesticides
- **Importance:** {{hl}}25%{{/hl}} crop losses due to pests
- **Concern:** {{hl}}0.1%{{/hl}} is used of applied reach their intended pest

• Fertilizers [4:2:1]
- **Consumption:** {{hl}}655 lakh tonnes{{/hl}} fertilizers in FY25
- **Use vs Productivity:** Fertilizers usage increased {{hl}}25 times since 1960{{/hl}} but food production increased by only {{hl}}3 times{{/hl}}.
- **Fiscal Burden:** Fertilizer accounts for large fiscal subsidies
    - &rupee;{{hl}}1.75 lakh crore{{/hl}} spent on fertilizer subsidies (2023-24).
    - {{hl}}2nd highest fiscal expense{{/hl}} after food
- **Imports:** ${{hl}}8.29 billion in 2024{{/hl}}-25
- **Targeting:** Only {{hl}}35%{{/hl}} reach beneficiaries
• Urea:
- In India, urea is the most produced, imported, consumed and physically regulated fertilizer of all.
- **Govt spending:** Govt spends &rupee;1,500 per bag of Urea, making it unsustainably cheap for farmers.
- India is the {{hl}}2nd largest consumer{{/hl}} of urea after China.
• DAP:
- **Import cost** is $636 (&rupee;55,150) per tonne, while production costs exceed &rupee;65,000 per tonne.
- **Subsidy Burden:** Govt caps DAP price at &rupee;27,000 per tonne, but the subsidy needed to cover costs is high.

• Storage
- Short of {{hl}}30-40 lakh{{/hl}} tones ([Ashok Dalwai](https://agricoop.nic.in/en/Doubling))

• Post Harvest Losses
- {{hl}}12% of total{{/hl}} agricultural GDP
- {{hl}}10% of total{{/hl}} food grain production ([ICAR](https://icar.org.in/))

• Exports
- Just {{hl}}2.4%{{/hl}} of world’s share [{{hl}}8th{{/hl}} rank]

• Farmer Suicides
- At least one farmer died by suicide every hour in India [[NCRB](https://ncrb.gov.in/)]

• Expense in R&D
- India spends about {{hl}}0.7%{{/hl}} of its agri -GDP on agri -research and Education (R&E)
- &rupee;1 investment in agri R&D can fetch &rupee;13 return [[Economic Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)].

• Machines
- Only {{hl}}40-45%{{/hl}} levels of mechanization
- India ↠ 1/{{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} of global tractors

• Crops and Yield
- Total kharif food grain production -> {{hl}}1647.05 lakh{{/hl}} metric tonnes (LMT) in 2024-25.
- India's rice yield -> {{hl}}2,191 kg{{/hl}} per hectare (global average {{hl}}3,026 kg{{/hl}} per hectare).
- Wheat yield -> {{hl}}2,750 kg{{/hl}}/hectare (global avg {{hl}}3,289 kg{{/hl}}/hectare).

• Cotton
- **Yield:** {{hl}}435kg{{/hl}}/hectare; similar to 2024-25’s yield of {{hl}}447kg{{/hl}}/hectare.
- **Rainfed crop:** {{hl}}67%{{/hl}} of India’s cotton is produced on rain-fed areas and {{hl}}33%{{/hl}} on irrigated lands
- **Acreage:** India ranks {{hl}}1st{{/hl}} in cotton acreage with around {{hl}}40%{{/hl}} of the world area under cotton
- **Production:** India ranks {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} in cotton production with estimated production of {{hl}}343.47 lakh{{/hl}} bales (5.84 MMT) in 2022-23 i.e. {{hl}}23.83%{{/hl}} of world cotton production.
- **Productivity:** {{hl}}39th rank{{/hl}} in overall cotton yield -> lower than countries like USA, China, Brazil etc.
- **Consumption:** {{hl}}2nd largest consumer{{/hl}} of cotton -> {{hl}}22.24%{{/hl}} of world cotton consumption (2023).
- **Exports:** {{hl}}30 lakh{{/hl}} bales i.e. {{hl}}6%{{/hl}} of world export in 2022-23.

• Oilseeds
- **Contribution:** India contributes about {{hl}}5-6%{{/hl}} of world production.
- **Area:** India accounts for {{hl}}15-20% of global{{/hl}} oilseed area
- **Rainfed:** {{hl}}76%{{/hl}} of oilseed cultivation is rainfed.
• National Mission on Edible oils- Targets for 2030-31:
- Increase primary oilseed production to {{hl}}69.7 million tonnes {{/hl}}(from {{hl}}39 million tonnes in 2022{{/hl}}-23).
- Expand oilseed cultivation by an additional {{hl}}40 lakh hectares{{/hl}} by targeting rice and potato fallow lands, promoting intercropping.

• Allied Sector: Fisheries
- **Production:** India is {{hl}}2nd largest fish producer{{/hl}}
- **Global:** {{hl}}8%{{/hl}} share in global fish production
    - India ranks {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} in aquaculture production, leads in shrimp production and {{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} in capture fisheries production.
- **Inland fisheries:** {{hl}}75% of total{{/hl}} fisheries output.
- **Growth Rate:** > {{hl}}10%{{/hl}} annually
• Contribution:
- {{hl}}1.25 %{{/hl}} of India GDP
- {{hl}}5%{{/hl}} of Agriculture’s GDP ([FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/))

• Allied Sector: Livestock
- India has the world’s largest livestock population
- Largest milk producer ({{hl}}23% of global{{/hl}} milk production).
- {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} in egg production, {{hl}}5th{{/hl}} in meat production ([FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/))
- **Economic contribution:** {{hl}}5.50%{{/hl}} of India’s Gross Value Added (GVA) in 2022-23.
- **Employment:** {{hl}}8.8 %{{/hl}} of the population; livelihood for {{hl}}70%{{/hl}} of rural households
- **Insurance:** Only {{hl}}15.47%{{/hl}} of animals are under insurance cover.
- **Productivity:** Average annual productivity of cattle in India is {{hl}}1777 kg{{/hl}}/animal/year (world average of {{hl}}2699 kg{{/hl}}/animal/year (2019-20)).
- **Methane emissions:** Enteric methane emission -> {{hl}}15.1%{{/hl}} total global enteric methane emission.

• Allied Sector: Horticulture
- **Contribution:** Contributes about {{hl}}33%{{/hl}} to the agriculture GVA
- **Production:** {{hl}}362.08 million tonnes {{/hl}}(Final Est. 2024-25; revised up to {{hl}}367.72 MT{{/hl}} as of Aug 2025, comprising {{hl}}114.51 MT{{/hl}} fruits and {{hl}}219.67 MT{{/hl}} vegetables) -> ~{{hl}}90% of total{{/hl}} horticulture production ([DAC&FW](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2248987®=3&lang=1) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
    - India is the {{hl}}2nd largest producer{{/hl}} of fruits and vegetables
    - **Share in Global market Exports:** mere {{hl}}1%{{/hl}}
    - **Exports:** India ranked {{hl}}14th{{/hl}} in vegetables and {{hl}}23rd{{/hl}} in fruits
    - India is the largest producer of Onions, ginger and okra among vegetables and ranks {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} in production of Potatoes, Cauliflowers, Brinjal, Cabbages, etc ([FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/))

• Organic Farming
- **No. of farmers:** India ranks {{hl}}1st{{/hl}} in terms of number of farmers -> Home to {{hl}}30% of total{{/hl}} organic producers
- **Area under Cultivation:** {{hl}}1.76 million hectares{{/hl}}
- **Certified area:** India ranks at {{hl}}4th place{{/hl}} in terms of certified area globally [International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements]
- **Sikkim:** {{hl}}1st{{/hl}} State in the world -> fully organic
- **Lakshadweep** is the only UT declared {{hl}}100%{{/hl}} organic.

• Food Processing
- India’s FPI is {{hl}}6th largest{{/hl}} in the world.
• Contribution:
- {{hl}}7.7%{{/hl}} to manufacturing GVA
- Valued at {{hl}}USD 160 billion{{/hl}}
- {{hl}}22.6%{{/hl}} in agri food exports
- **Growth Rate:** > {{hl}}10%{{/hl}}
- {{hl}}75%{{/hl}} of industry is unorganized
- **FDI:** {{hl}}100%{{/hl}} FDI in food processing under automatic route and {{hl}}100%{{/hl}} FDI in trading, including e-commerce.
- **Potential:** Indian food processing industry to reach ${{hl}}700 billion by 2030{{/hl}}.

• Public Distribution System
- **NFSA 2013:** Covers {{hl}}67% of population{{/hl}}
    - **Rural Area:** {{hl}}75%{{/hl}}
    - **Urban Area:** {{hl}}50%{{/hl}}
- **Beneficiaries of NFSA (PMGKAY):** {{hl}}80.56 crore{{/hl}} beneficiaries identified out of targeted {{hl}}81.35 crore {{/hl}}(free foodgrains extended for {{hl}}5 years{{/hl}} from Jan 2024 to Dec 2028) ([DFPD](https://dfpd.gov.in/)).
    - {{hl}}80.56 cr{{/hl}} people have been identified, out of the targeted {{hl}}81.35 cr{{/hl}}
    - **Food Subsidy Expense:** {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} of India's total subsidy spending in FY 2024-25
    - **Fair Price Shops:** > 5 Lac shops are there with almost {{hl}}100%{{/hl}} automation.

• Mining
- **Contribution:** B/w {{hl}}2.2%{{/hl}} and {{hl}}2.5%{{/hl}} of India’s GDP
- **Employment:** approximately {{hl}}1.3 million{{/hl}} people
- **Mine closure:** An average of 100 mine workers per day face potential unemployment by 2035 due to mine closure (Global Energy Monitor)

content_markdown:
SECONDARY SECTOR

• Manufacturing
- **Current:** ~{{hl}}17%{{/hl}} of GVA (Manufacturing GVA grew by {{hl}}7.72%{{/hl}} in Q1 and {{hl}}9.13%{{/hl}} in Q2 of FY26; Industry GVA grew {{hl}}7.0%{{/hl}} in H1 FY26) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
    - **Potential:** {{hl}}27%{{/hl}} by 2047.

    - **Targets** as per National Manufacturing Policy (NMP), 2011
        - **GDP Share of Manufacturing:** {{hl}}25% of GDP{{/hl}} by 2025
        - **Employment in Manufacturing:** ~{{hl}}10 crore{{/hl}} jobs by 2025
    - **India Vs China:** India holds {{hl}}2.8%{{/hl}} of the global manufacturing share, compared to China's {{hl}}28.8%{{/hl}}.

• Industry Sector
- {{hl}}27 - 29% of GDP{{/hl}}
- {{hl}}25%{{/hl}} of workforce is employed ([ILO 2023](https://www.ilo.org/sites/default/files/wcmsp5/groups/public/@dgreports/@dcomm/@publ/documents/publication/wcms_711919.pdf))

• MSME
- {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} Largest employer after Agriculture
- {{hl}}29%{{/hl}} to India's GDP [Potential: {{hl}}40%{{/hl}} to GDP by 2030]
- {{hl}}40%{{/hl}} of Exports
- Employing {{hl}}7.5 crore{{/hl}} people
- {{hl}}62%{{/hl}} to employment in India (McKinsey Global Institute)
- {{hl}}95%{{/hl}} firms → Unorganised
- **Registered MSMEs:** >{{hl}}5.93 crore{{/hl}} registered on Udyam portal ([Ministry of MSME 2025](https://udyamregistration.gov.in/))
    - **MSMEs on e-Commerce Platforms:** Only {{hl}}6%{{/hl}} of MSMEs actively use e- commerce platforms for sales.
• PM Mudra Yojana: MSMEs
- **Accounts:** {{hl}}55.45 crore{{/hl}} loan accounts sanctioned as of October 2025 (up from ~{{hl}}35 crore{{/hl}}) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
- **Credit support:** disbursed over {{hl}}₹36.18 lakh crore{{/hl}} as of October 2025 (up from {{hl}}₹18.39 lakh crore{{/hl}}) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
    - **Women entrepreneurs:** {{hl}}71.4 % of total{{/hl}} no. of accounts (FY 2022).
    - **Categories:** Majority loan accounts (~{{hl}}80%{{/hl}}) are in the Shishu category (FY 2021), followed by Kishore at {{hl}}18.70 %{{/hl}}.

• Special Economic Zone (SEZ)
- India has 280 Operational SEZs (Nov 2024)
- **Employment:** {{hl}}2.8 million{{/hl}} jobs.
- **Exports:** ${{hl}}163.69 billion in 2023{{/hl}}-24

• Electronics Sector
- **India’s share in Global Electronics Market:** only {{hl}}4%{{/hl}}
- **Electronics Production:** {{hl}}₹9.52 lakh crore in FY24{{/hl}} (crossed {{hl}}₹11.5 lakh crore in FY25{{/hl}}; PLI schemes across 14 sectors attracted >{{hl}}₹2.0 lakh crore{{/hl}} investment, generating >{{hl}}₹18.7 lakh crore{{/hl}} production and >{{hl}}12.6 lakh{{/hl}} jobs as of Sep 2025) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
    - **Mobile phones:** India is {{hl}}2nd largest mobile phone{{/hl}} producer in World.
        - {{hl}}325 million{{/hl}}+ mobile phones manufactured in India every year.
        - {{hl}}99%{{/hl}} of smartphones sold in India are now made domestically.
    - **Exports:** Expected to reach $120 Bn by FY26.
    - CAGR of around {{hl}}25%{{/hl}} through 2028.
- **Semiconductor Market:** Projected to grow at {{hl}}13%{{/hl}} reaching {{hl}}₹8.9 lakh crore by 2030{{/hl}}
- India Semiconductor Mission approved 10 projects across 6 states worth {{hl}}₹1.60 lakh crore {{/hl}}(ISM 2.0 announced in [Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf) / [Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).

• Pharmaceutical
- {{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} Largest by volume, {{hl}}14th{{/hl}} Largest by value
- **Generic Medicines:** India is the largest manufacturer of generic medicines globally.
- **Economic Contribution:** {{hl}}1.72%{{/hl}} to the GDP [Projected to reach {{hl}}USD 130 billion by 2030{{/hl}}]
    - **Market Value:** ${{hl}}50 billion.{{/hl}}
- **Vaccines:** India supplies over {{hl}}50% of global{{/hl}} vaccine demand
- **Exports:** India ranks {{hl}}12th globally{{/hl}} in medical goods exports
- **US Imports:** US imports {{hl}}USD 9 billion{{/hl}} worth of pharma formulations from India annually.

• Toy Industry
- **Market value:** 1.5 Billion USD in 2023
    - Projected to increase to ${{hl}}3 billion by 2028{{/hl}}
- **Exports:** {{hl}}USD 326 million{{/hl}} to {{hl}}USD 348 million{{/hl}} for the last three years.
    - **India's Share:** {{hl}}0.3%{{/hl}} in 2022; **China:** {{hl}}80%{{/hl}}

• Textile Industry
- **GDP:** {{hl}}2.3%{{/hl}} to India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) [Projected to reach {{hl}}5%{{/hl}} by 2030].
- **Employs** {{hl}}4.5 crore{{/hl}} workers [After agriculture, textiles and apparel form the second-largest employer in India]
- **Exports:** {{hl}}8.21%{{/hl}} of India’s total merchandise exports
    - India is the {{hl}}6th largest exporter{{/hl}} of textiles and apparel globally ([Eco Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/))
    - **India’s global trade share:** {{hl}}4%{{/hl}} in textiles and apparel
- **Capacity:** {{hl}}2nd largest textile manufacturing{{/hl}} capacity globally
- **FDI:** {{hl}}100%{{/hl}} FDI allowed in textiles under the automatic route.
• Fabric Production [India]
- Silk → {{hl}}2nd largest producer{{/hl}}
- Cotton → {{hl}}2nd largest producer{{/hl}}
- Jute → largest producer
- Man-Made fibres (MMF) → largest producer

• Sugar Industry
- **India as Consumer:** Largest in World
- **India as Producer:** {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} Largest in World
- **India as Exporter:** {{hl}}3rd largest{{/hl}} in World (typos fixed: {{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} -> {{hl}}3rd{{/hl}})
    - **India’s Share in Global Sugar Production:** {{hl}}19%{{/hl}}
    - **Employment:** Livelihood for {{hl}}5 crore{{/hl}} farmers and their families.

• Steel Industry
- **India as Consumer:** {{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} Largest in World after China and USA.
- **India as Producer:** {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} Largest in World of crude steel
- **FDI:** {{hl}}100%{{/hl}} FDI allowed under the automatic route.
- **Finished steel consumption (Per capita):** 97.7 kgs (2023-24)
- **Capital-Intensive Sector:** INR {{hl}}7,000 crore{{/hl}} is required to set up 1 tonne of steel- making capacity through the greenfield route.

• Make in India Progress
- **Toy:** India produces {{hl}}400 million{{/hl}} Toys annually
- **Mobiles:** India is the second-largest mobile manufacturer in the world
• Ease of Doing Business
- India climbed from {{hl}}142nd{{/hl}} in 2014 to {{hl}}63rd{{/hl}} in the World Bank's Doing Business Report (DBR), 2020 before its discontinuation.
- Over 40000 compliances have been reduced and 3,800 provisions decriminalized.

content_markdown:
TERTIARY SECTOR

• Service Sector
- **Economic contribution:** {{hl}}56.4%{{/hl}} of GVA in FY26 FAE (highest ever; {{hl}}53.6% of GDP{{/hl}} in H1 FY26, ~{{hl}}55% of GDP{{/hl}} overall) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
    - **Potential:** By 2047, the services sector is expected to contribute {{hl}}60 per cent{{/hl}} of India’s GDP.
    - {{hl}}30%{{/hl}} of the Workforce ([Eco survey 24-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/))
- **Growth Rate:** Estimated at {{hl}}9.1%{{/hl}} in FY26 ({{hl}}9.3%{{/hl}} in H1 FY26), after >{{hl}}6%{{/hl}} annual growth over the past decade ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
    - **Exports:** India ranked {{hl}}7th worldwide{{/hl}} in global services exports
- **India's share in Global Services Exports:** {{hl}}4.3%{{/hl}} in CY 2024 (more than doubled from {{hl}}2%{{/hl}} in 2005; services exports hit record {{hl}}USD 387.6 billion in FY25{{/hl}} and {{hl}}USD 421.3 billion in FY26{{/hl}}) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf) / [MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
    - **IT, Computer services and Business Services Exports:** ~{{hl}}70%{{/hl}} of India's services exports.

• IT Sector
- India is {{hl}}2nd largest{{/hl}} Exporter of Software, after USA (typo fixed: {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}} -> {{hl}}2nd{{/hl}})
    - **Contribution:** {{hl}}7.5%{{/hl}} of India's GDP (as of FY23)
        - Projected to hit {{hl}}10%{{/hl}} by FY25
    - **Outsourcing market:** India is a leading exporter of IT and BPM services, holding about {{hl}}56%{{/hl}} of the global outsourcing market.
    - **Market potential:** Domestic software market is projected to hit ${{hl}}100 billion by 2035{{/hl}} [SaaS Boomi report]

• Tourism
- {{hl}}5% of GDP{{/hl}}
- **Employment:** {{hl}}7.6 crore{{/hl}} jobs in FY23 | {{hl}}7%{{/hl}} of Employment
- **Travel & Tourism Development Index (TTDI) 2024:** 39/119
- **Inbound visitor markets for India in 2023:** Bangladesh ({{hl}}9%{{/hl}}), the United States ({{hl}}9%{{/hl}}), and the United Kingdom ({{hl}}6%{{/hl}}).

• E-Commerce
- **Share:** Around {{hl}}8% of total{{/hl}} Retail market [2023-24]
    - up from {{hl}}4–5%{{/hl}} in 2018–19
- **Growth Rate:** More than {{hl}}20% {{/hl}}[That is a CAGR of {{hl}}27%{{/hl}}]
- **Potential:** India’s E-commerce market is expected to grow to ${{hl}}325 billion by 2030{{/hl}} [[Invest India](https://www.investindia.gov.in/india-fdi-investment-key-sectors)]

• FinTech
- India ranks as {{hl}}3rd largest and fastest-growing{{/hl}} fintech market globally.
- **India’s fintech adoption rate:** {{hl}}87%{{/hl}}
- Account for {{hl}}70%{{/hl}} of digital payment transactions.
- **Growth Rate:** More than {{hl}}30% {{/hl}}[That is a CAGR of {{hl}}30.26%{{/hl}}]

• Telecommunication
- India is the world’s {{hl}}2nd largest telecommunications{{/hl}} market.
- **Telephone Subscriber Base:** {{hl}}133.06 crore {{/hl}}({{hl}}1,330.58 million{{/hl}}) as of March 2026 (up from {{hl}}120.08 crore{{/hl}} in March 2025) [[TRAI Yearly Performance Indicators 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
- **Overall Tele-Density:** {{hl}}93.26%{{/hl}} as of March 2026 ({{hl}}86.76%{{/hl}} in late 2025; {{hl}}84.57%{{/hl}} excluding M2M) [[TRAI 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
- **Urban tele-density:** {{hl}}151.47%{{/hl}} as of March 2026 (up from {{hl}}131.45%{{/hl}} in March 2025) [[TRAI 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
- **Rural tele-density:** {{hl}}60.46%{{/hl}} as of March 2026 (up from {{hl}}59.06%{{/hl}} in March 2025) [[TRAI 2025-26](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2319321®=48&lang=1)]
    - Delhi Service area has maximum tele-density of {{hl}}274.59%{{/hl}}
    - Bihar service area has minimum tele-density of {{hl}}56.90%{{/hl}}
    - **FDI:** {{hl}}4th largest sector{{/hl}} in terms of FDI inflows, contributing {{hl}}6% of total{{/hl}} FDI inflow.

subject: INDIAN ECONOMY
content_markdown:
INCLUSIVE GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT

• Inclusive Growth
- India ranks {{hl}}62nd{{/hl}} out of 74 emerging countries [[Inclusive Development Index, WEF](https://www.weforum.org/)].

• Employment & Unemployment
- **Total Workforce:** {{hl}}56.2–56.5 crore{{/hl}} employed (aged 15+ years in Q2 FY26; over {{hl}}31 crore{{/hl}} unorganised workers registered on e-Shram portal as of Jan 2026, {{hl}}54%{{/hl}} women) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
    - **Need of Jobs:** Indian Economy needs to generate nearly {{hl}}78.5 lakh{{/hl}} jobs annually(non-farm sector) until 2030 to cater need of rising workforce.
- **Unemployment Rate:** {{hl}}5.1%{{/hl}} in monthly PLFS (April 2025); annual usual status (ps+ss) UR stood at {{hl}}3.2% {{/hl}}(female UR at {{hl}}2.1%{{/hl}}) ([MoSPI PLFS Annual Report 2025](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/publications_reports/publications_reports1780040415321_0624fb13-fb47-40bc-b470-7c7e9635c3ef_PLFS_2025_F_REV_29052026.pdf))
    - **Self-Employed Workers:** It has grown from {{hl}}52.2%{{/hl}} in 2017-18 to {{hl}}58.4%{{/hl}} in 2023-24.
    - **Govt Jobs:** {{hl}}7%{{/hl}} of Total employment
    - **Informal Sector:** {{hl}}90%{{/hl}}
    - **Net EPFO Subscriptions:** more than doubling from {{hl}}61 lakh in FY19{{/hl}} to {{hl}}131 lakhs in FY24{{/hl}}.

• Gig Economy
- **Total:** Employ over {{hl}}12 million{{/hl}} workers [{{hl}}1.5% of total{{/hl}} Workforce]
    - Projected to reach {{hl}}23.5 million by 2029{{/hl}}–30 [[NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf)]
- **Job creation:** Out of 100 New Jobs, 56 are being created in Gig sector.

• Education & Skills
• Stream wise Ratio:
- Humanities ({{hl}}33%{{/hl}}), Science ({{hl}}15%{{/hl}}), Commerce ({{hl}}14%{{/hl}}), English ({{hl}}12%{{/hl}})
- **Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR):** Steady at 23:1 for the last five years.
- **University Density (per 1 lakh eligible students):** Highest in Sikkim (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (5.6), Ladakh (5.2), etc. In Bihar (0.2), UP (0.3), West Bengal & Maharashtra (0.6) the density is below national average.
• Government Spending:
- **Expenditure:** {{hl}}2.9% of GDP{{/hl}}
    - Target under NEP 2020: {{hl}}6% of GDP{{/hl}}
- **Budgetary allocation:** {{hl}}₹1.39 lakh crore {{/hl}}({{hl}}₹1,39,289 crore{{/hl}}) allocated to the Ministry of Education in Union Budget 2026-27 (up {{hl}}8.27%{{/hl}} from {{hl}}₹1.28 lakh crore in 2025{{/hl}}-26) ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455)).
• Inefficient Infrastructure [[UDISE+ 2023-24 Report](https://udiseplus.gov.in/)]
- **Computers:** The percentage of schools having computers ↑ from {{hl}}38.5 %{{/hl}} in 2019-20 to {{hl}}57.2 %{{/hl}} in 2023-2024.
- **Internet:** Percentage of schools having internet facility increased from {{hl}}22.3 %{{/hl}} in 2019-20 to {{hl}}53.9 %{{/hl}} in 2023-2024.
- **Electricity:** Of the over {{hl}}14.71 lakh{{/hl}} schools in India, up to {{hl}}1.52 lakh{{/hl}} schools have no functional electricity.
- **Drinking Water:** While {{hl}}14.47 lakh{{/hl}} schools claim to have drinking water facilities, only {{hl}}14.11 lakh{{/hl}} have them functional.
- **Toilets:** Government schools constitute the majority of the 67,000 schools operating without functional toilets.
- **Differently-Abled Students:** Only {{hl}}33.2%{{/hl}} of government schools have disabled-friendly toilets.
- **Digital Education:** {{hl}}46 %{{/hl}} schools have functional computers ([Ministry of Education](https://www.education.gov.in/))
• Universities and Colleges:
- **Institutions:** Total Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) increased from 51,534 in 2014-15 to 70,018 as of June 2025 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) [1,168 universities, 45,473 colleges and 12,002 stand-alone institutions in AISHE 2021-22].
    - **Accreditation:** Only {{hl}}37% of universities{{/hl}} are accredited
    - **Growth:** In last {{hl}}10 years{{/hl}}, number of universities has increased by {{hl}}60%{{/hl}}, colleges up {{hl}}21% {{/hl}}[[Ministry of Education](https://www.education.gov.in/)]
    - **Increased Penetration in Rural Areas:** {{hl}}43%{{/hl}} Universities and {{hl}}61.4%{{/hl}} colleges are located in Rural Areas.
    - **Institutes of National Importance (INIs):** 171 [June 2024]
    - **Medical Colleges:** {{hl}}102%{{/hl}} increase-> rising from 387 before 2014 to 780 in 2024
        - **Increase in MBBS seats:** {{hl}}130%{{/hl}} rise in MBBS seats
    - **IIMs:** 21
    - **IITs:** 23
• Startup:
- **Definition:** An entity, HQ in India, opened less than {{hl}}10 years{{/hl}} ago, and annual turnover < &rupee;{{hl}}100 crore.{{/hl}}
- **Recognized startups:** DPIIT-recognized startups increased from ~500 (2016) to over {{hl}}2.23 lakh{{/hl}} as of March 31, 2026 (up from {{hl}}1.59 lakh{{/hl}} in early 2025) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)).
    - **Positive Ecosystem:** {{hl}}3rd largest startup ecosystem{{/hl}} in India
    - **High Failure Rate:** {{hl}}90%{{/hl}} fail within {{hl}}5 years{{/hl}}.
- **Employment Generation:** Recognized startups have created over {{hl}}23.36 lakh{{/hl}} direct jobs as of March 31, 2026 (up from {{hl}}16.6 lakh{{/hl}} in Oct 2024) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2))
- **Women Entrepreneurship:** Over {{hl}}1.07 lakh{{/hl}} recognized startups have at least one woman director/partner as of March 31, 2026 (~{{hl}}48%{{/hl}} of [DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)-recognised startups, up from 73,151) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [PIB 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2)).
• Pain Points:
• Higher Education:
- Only {{hl}}42.6%{{/hl}} of Indian graduates are employable [India's Graduate Skill Index 2025]
• QS World Rankings 2025: Top Indian Institutes
- No Institute in TOP 100
- **IIT Bombay:** Leading in India, IIT Bombay climbed from {{hl}}149th{{/hl}} in 2024 to {{hl}}118th{{/hl}} in 2025.
- **IIT Delhi:** Achieved the second position in India, moving up 47 ranks from {{hl}}197th{{/hl}} to {{hl}}150th{{/hl}}.
• Schools:
• ASER 2024
- **Reading skill:** {{hl}}76.6%{{/hl}} of Class 3 students still cannot read Class 2 text.
- **Foundational Numeracy Skills:** Over {{hl}}50% of students{{/hl}} (14-18 age) face difficulties with elementary division problems.
- **Arithmetic:** {{hl}}66.3%{{/hl}} of Class 3 students and {{hl}}70%{{/hl}} of Class 5 students cannot perform simple arithmetic calculations.
- Class 3 students able to do subtraction is just {{hl}}33.7%{{/hl}} in 2024.
- **Vocational Training:** Only about {{hl}}2%{{/hl}} have received formal vocational training [Ministry of Skill Development]
• Problem in Basic Skills:
- **NCERT Report 2022:** {{hl}}11%{{/hl}} of Class 3 students in India lack basic skills in Mathematics.

• Skill (General State)
- **Formally Skilled Workforce:** < {{hl}}5%{{/hl}}
    - South Korea: {{hl}}95%{{/hl}}
    - Japan: {{hl}}80%{{/hl}}
    - Germany: {{hl}}75%{{/hl}}
    - USA: {{hl}}50%{{/hl}}
- **Employability of Graduates:** Only {{hl}}51%{{/hl}} graduates employable [[Economic Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)]
- **Vocational Training to Workforce:** {{hl}}65.3%{{/hl}} has received no form of vocational training [[Economic Survey 2024-25](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/)]
- **Low Formal Training:** only {{hl}}2.7%{{/hl}} of India’s workforce has received formal skill training, compared to {{hl}}52%{{/hl}} in US, {{hl}}80%{{/hl}} in Japan, and {{hl}}96%{{/hl}} in South Korea.

• Deeptech Startup ecosystem
- **Global Standing:** Despite having the {{hl}}3rd largest pool{{/hl}} of DeepTech startups, India ranked {{hl}}6th among the top{{/hl}} 9 DeepTech ecosystems in the world in 2023 (Nasscom).

• Insurance
- **Insurance Penetration:** {{hl}}3.7% of GDP{{/hl}} in FY24 [Global average: {{hl}}7%{{/hl}}]
    - Life Insurance penetration: {{hl}}2.8%{{/hl}}
    - Non-Life insurance remained at {{hl}}1%{{/hl}}.
- India ranks {{hl}}10th{{/hl}} in the global life insurance market.

• Pension Sector
- **Participation:** Only about {{hl}}12%{{/hl}} of the Indian workforce participates in any formal pension scheme.
- **NPS & APY Coverage:** Combined National Pension System (NPS) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY) subscribers cover approximately {{hl}}5.3%{{/hl}} of India’s population as of early 2025.

• Poverty
• India – Poverty
- **Percentage:** {{hl}}21.9%{{/hl}} {2011, Tendulkar Report}
- **Extreme poverty:** Under the World Bank's revised International Poverty Line ($3.00/day at 2021 PPP, up from $2.15/day), India's extreme poverty rate stood at {{hl}}5.3%{{/hl}} in 2022-23 (and {{hl}}23.9%{{/hl}} at the lower-middle-income line) [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)]
• Decrease in Poverty [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]
- **Extreme Poverty Lift:** 171 Million lifted from Extreme Poverty in last decade.
- {{hl}}India’s Poverty Rate (at the 3.65 dollars per day line) ->{{/hl}} Fell from {{hl}}61.8 percent in 2011{{/hl}}-12 to {{hl}}28.1 percent in 2022{{/hl}}-23.
    - Rural poverty declined from {{hl}}69 percent{{/hl}} to {{hl}}32.5 percent{{/hl}}
    - Urban poverty dropped from {{hl}}43.5 percent{{/hl}} to {{hl}}17.2 percent{{/hl}}.
- **Non-monetary poverty (Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)) ->** declined from {{hl}}55.3%{{/hl}} in 2005-06 to {{hl}}11.28%{{/hl}} in 2022-23 ([NITI Aayog](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-08/India-National-Multidimentional-Poverty-Index-2023.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) [[UNDP](https://hdr.undp.org/) MPI: {{hl}}53.8%{{/hl}} in 2005-06 to {{hl}}16.4%{{/hl}} in 2019-21].
• Global – Poverty
- **Incidence:** {{hl}}8.5% of total{{/hl}} population i.e. {{hl}}75 cr{{/hl}} live in extreme poverty - on less than $2.15 per day [[World Bank](https://data.worldbank.org/country/india)]
- **Deprived Regions:** 5 out of 6 poor are in Sub-Saharan or South Asia
- **Rural > Urban –** over {{hl}}75%{{/hl}} of all poor live in rural areas.
- **High Prevalence among Children (< 18):** {{hl}}50% of total{{/hl}} poor
• Global Inequality ([Oxfam](https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/takers-not-makers-unjust-poverty-and-unearned-wealth-colonialism)):
- The richest {{hl}}1%{{/hl}} control {{hl}}45% of global{{/hl}} wealth.
- {{hl}}44%{{/hl}} of the world's population lives below the World Bank's poverty line of $6.85 (PPP).
• India Inequality ([Oxfam](https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/takers-not-makers-unjust-poverty-and-unearned-wealth-colonialism)):
- Richest {{hl}}1%{{/hl}} control more than {{hl}}40% of total{{/hl}} wealth
- Bottom {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} own merely {{hl}}3%{{/hl}} 3. Gini Index
• Gini Coefficient:
- The Gini coefficient improved for rural areas (declined to 0.237 in 2023-24 from 0.266 in 2022-23) and urban areas (declined to 0.284 in 2023-24 from 0.314 in 2022-23).

• Hunger
• Status of Hunger [[Global Hunger Index 2024](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]
• Global:
- {{hl}}2.8 billion{{/hl}} people cannot afford a healthy diet.
• India Specific:
- **India's Rank:** Improved to {{hl}}102nd{{/hl}} out of 123 countries in Global Hunger Index 2025 (up from {{hl}}105th{{/hl}} out of 127 in GHI 2024; remains in the "serious" category) [[GHI 2025](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]
    - **Child Wasting Rate:** {{hl}}18.7% {{/hl}}[Highest in World]
- **Stunted Children:** {{hl}}32.9%{{/hl}} in GHI 2025 (down from >{{hl}}35%{{/hl}} earlier;Child Wasting remains {{hl}}18.7%{{/hl}}) [[GHI 2025](https://www.globalhungerindex.org/pdf/en/2025.pdf)]
    - **Under-5 mortality:** {{hl}}2.9%{{/hl}}
    - Status of Food Security [[State of Food Security and Nutrition Report (2024)](https://www.fao.org/publications/home/fao-flagship-publications/the-state-of-food-security-and-nutrition-in-the-world)]
• India Specific:
- **Undernourished:** {{hl}}13%{{/hl}} from Chronic Undernourishment
- **Anemic:** {{hl}}53%{{/hl}} of Women
• UN-FAO Report:
- Hunger in India came down to {{hl}}13.7%{{/hl}} during 2021-23 period

• Regional Disparity
- **Delhi’s per capita Income** = {{hl}}2.5 times{{/hl}} of national average [[EAC-PM](https://eacpm.gov.in/)]
- Rural-Urban Inequality [[Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports)]
    - **Rural Area:** &rupee;4,122 MPCE
    - **Urban Area:** &rupee;6,996 MPCE [Higher by around {{hl}}70%{{/hl}}]

NATIONAL INCOME & ACCOUNTING

- Real GDP grew by {{hl}}7.4%{{/hl}} in FY26 (FAE) after {{hl}}6.5%{{/hl}} growth in FY25 ({{hl}}₹187.97 lakh crore{{/hl}}) ([MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1767781372753_1380ce82-f5a5-440d-99e6-e6b35af0deb5_GDP_Press_Note_on_FAE_2025-26.pdf) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))

- **India's Retail Inflation (CPI):** Dropped sharply to a series-low average of {{hl}}1.7%{{/hl}} in FY26 (April–December 2025), down from {{hl}}4.9%{{/hl}} in Apr–Dec 2024 and {{hl}}5.4%{{/hl}} in FY24 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).

- **Household Financial Savings** to reach {{hl}}6.5%{{/hl}} of Gross national disposable income (GNDI) in FY25 [[SBI report](https://sbi.co.in/web/corporate-governance/ecowrap)]

• Fiscal Policy & Government Budget
• Debt Profile
- **Government Debt to GDP** (Centre and states) - {{hl}}around 83.1%{{/hl}} (by 2024 end)
- **Central Government [Debt to GDP]** – Estimated at {{hl}}56.1%{{/hl}} in RE 2025-26 and {{hl}}55.6%{{/hl}} in BE 2026-27 (down from {{hl}}57.1%{{/hl}} in 2024-25) ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455))

    - **State Government [Debt to GDP]** – {{hl}}26%{{/hl}}
• Debt of the Central Government:
- **Internal debt:** {{hl}}94%{{/hl}}
- **Public Debt:** {{hl}}89.9%{{/hl}}
- **External Debt:** {{hl}}6%{{/hl}}
- **External Debt to GDP Ratio:** In India, external debt constituted {{hl}}19.4%{{/hl}} of the total GDP at the end of September 2024.
    - Across currencies, the external debt remained primarily denominated in the US Dollar ({{hl}}53.4 %{{/hl}}), followed by the INR ({{hl}}31.2 %{{/hl}}), SDR ({{hl}}5 %{{/hl}}), and the Euro ({{hl}}3 %{{/hl}}).

• Foreign Trade
- **India's Total Exports:** Scaled an all-time high of {{hl}}$863.1 billion in FY 2025-26{{/hl}} (${{hl}}441.8B{{/hl}} merchandise + ${{hl}}421.3B{{/hl}} services), up from ${{hl}}825.3 billion in FY 2024{{/hl}}-25 ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
    - **Exports in 2016:** It was around {{hl}}USD 435 billion in FY 2016{{/hl}}.
    - **India’s target** for export is USD 2 Trillion by 2030.
• Trade
- **Deficit:** Overall trade deficit -> {{hl}}USD 78.1 billion in FY24{{/hl}} ([Eco Survey 2023-24](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2024-25/economicsurvey/index.php)).
- **Largest Trade Deficit:** China [${{hl}}112.6 billion in FY 2025{{/hl}}-26, up from ${{hl}}99.2 billion in FY 2024{{/hl}}-25] ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
- **Largest Trading Partner:** China surpassed the USA in FY 2025-26 (in FY 2024-25, USA was {{hl}}1st{{/hl}} with ${{hl}}131.84 billion{{/hl}} bilateral trade and ${{hl}}40.89B{{/hl}} surplus; in FY26, India-US trade surplus was ${{hl}}34.4B{{/hl}}) ([MoC&I](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2290437®=48&lang=1))
    - **India’s Top Export Destinations:** USA ({{hl}}17.90%{{/hl}}) > UAE ({{hl}}8.23%{{/hl}}) > Netherlands ({{hl}}5.16%{{/hl}}) > China ({{hl}}3.85%{{/hl}}) > Singapore ({{hl}}3.33%{{/hl}}).
    - **India’s Top Import Source Nations:** China > UAE > USA > Russia.
• Remittances:
- India is the **largest recipient** of remittances globally
- **Remittances Received:** Record {{hl}}$135.4 billion in FY25{{/hl}} (${{hl}}129.4 billion in CY 2024{{/hl}}) ([RBI](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63744) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
    - The U.S. accounts for {{hl}}27.7%{{/hl}} of India's inward remittances

• Current Account Deficit (CAD)
- **CAD:** Moderated to {{hl}}0.8% of GDP{{/hl}} in H1 FY26 (from {{hl}}1.3%{{/hl}} in H1 FY25; ~{{hl}}1.3%{{/hl}} in Q2 FY26) ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))

• Forex Reserves
- {{hl}}US $701.4 billion{{/hl}} as of 16 January 2026 ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) and {{hl}}US $734.6 billion{{/hl}} as of 2 October 2026 ([RBI](https://m.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63744)), providing ~{{hl}}11 months{{/hl}} of import cover and {{hl}}94.4%{{/hl}} external debt cover.
    - **Import Cover:** It is sufficient to provide an import cover of more than {{hl}}11 months{{/hl}}.

• Investment

• FDI
- **Total FDI inflows** -> ${{hl}}81.04 billion in FY 2024{{/hl}}-25 (${{hl}}64.7 billion{{/hl}} in Apr–Nov 2025; total FDI inflows touched ${{hl}}94.53 billion {{/hl}}/ equity ${{hl}}58.85 billion in FY 2025{{/hl}}-26) ([DPIIT](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2253019®=3&lang=2) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)).
    - India's FDI inflows have increased ~{{hl}}20 times{{/hl}} from 2000-01 to 2023-24.
    - **Highest FDI Inflow:** Computer software and hardware.
    - **FDI Source:** Mauritius({{hl}}25%{{/hl}}) > Singapore ({{hl}}23%{{/hl}}) > USA ({{hl}}9%{{/hl}})
    - **FDI Top Destinations [FY 2024–25]:** Maharashtra ({{hl}}39%{{/hl}}) > Karnataka ({{hl}}13%{{/hl}}) > Delhi ({{hl}}12%{{/hl}})

• FPI
- **FPI Outflows:** FPIs have pulled out a massive &rupee;{{hl}}1.16 lakh crore{{/hl}} from Indian equities so far in 2025.

• Infrastructure - General
- **Current Investment:** Public capital expenditure increased to {{hl}}₹12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026-27 BE{{/hl}} (up from {{hl}}₹11.21 lakh crore in FY 2025{{/hl}}-26 BE; effective capex {{hl}}₹15.48 lakh crore in FY26{{/hl}} BE) ([Union Budget 2026-27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2221455) / [Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))
    - **Investment Required:** India will need to spend around {{hl}}₹143 trillion by 2030{{/hl}} on infrastructure.
    - **National Infrastructure Pipeline:** The projected infrastructure investment is {{hl}}₹111 trillion{{/hl}} for 2021-25 (over {{hl}}5 yrs{{/hl}}).
• Status of NIP [As of March 2025]:
- Planned investments rose from {{hl}}₹111 trillion{{/hl}} to {{hl}}₹168.93 trillion.{{/hl}}
- Completed investments are {{hl}}₹31.1 trillion{{/hl}}, achieving {{hl}}28%{{/hl}} of original target.

• Transport Sector

• Airways

- {{hl}}8th biggest passenger{{/hl}} traffic.

- **UDAN scheme:** {{hl}}679 routes connecting 95 airports{{/hl}}, heliports, and water aerodromes operationalised, benefiting >{{hl}}1.68 crore{{/hl}} passengers as of July 2026 (Modified UDAN approved in March 2026 with {{hl}}₹28,840 crore{{/hl}} outlay for FY27–FY36) ([MoCA](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) / [PIB Aug 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).

• Gas Based Economy
- **Aim:** PM aims to raise India's natural gas share from {{hl}}6.2%{{/hl}} to {{hl}}15%{{/hl}} by 2030 (World Avg: {{hl}}24.42%{{/hl}})
- **Import dependence:** around {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} of our requirement of Natural gas.
- **Import bill:** ${{hl}}15.2 billion in FY25{{/hl}}.

• SDGs
- **UN Sustainable Development Report 2026:** India achieved its highest-ever rank of {{hl}}94th out of 167 countries{{/hl}} (score 68.3), improving from {{hl}}99th{{/hl}} in SDR 2025 and {{hl}}109th{{/hl}} in SDR 2024 [[UN SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026](https://dashboards.sdgindex.org/profiles/india/)]

content_markdown:
CLIMATE CHANGE

Temperature Rise
- Planet already warmed at least 1.1 degrees Celsius
- {{hl}}77%{{/hl}} of climate experts expect temperature rise > 2.5° by 2100

Rising sea levels
- Risen by over {{hl}}10 cm{{/hl}} between 1993 and 2024 ([NASA](https://climate.nasa.gov/))
- **Projection:** Global mean SLR of 1.3-1.6 m by 2100 in high-emission scenario ([IPCC](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/)).

Carbon emissions
- {{hl}}Global average CO2 emissions->{{/hl}} 419.3 parts per million in 2023.
- **India (per capita):** {{hl}}1.9 ton{{/hl}} v/s {{hl}}4.7 ton {{/hl}}(World avg)
- {{hl}}World 3rd largest emitter{{/hl}} (after China, USA)

Greenhouse Gas Emissions [UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2024 & 2025]
- **Ranking:** India ranks {{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} in total GHG emissions (4,140 MtCO2e) [China ({{hl}}1st{{/hl}}) & US ({{hl}}2nd{{/hl}})].
- **Meeting climate ambition:** To limit global warming to 1.5°C (UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 'Off Target' puts cuts needed from 2019 levels at {{hl}}55%{{/hl}} by 2035 for 1.5°C and {{hl}}35%{{/hl}} by 2035 for 2°C; EGR 2024 cited {{hl}}42%{{/hl}} by 2030 and {{hl}}57%{{/hl}} by 2035):
    - Nations must cut {{hl}}42 %{{/hl}} off annual GHG emissions by 2030 and {{hl}}57 %{{/hl}} by 2035 in the next NDCs. {{hl}}5. Warmest year on record: 2024 ({{/hl}}[NOAA](https://www.noaa.gov/)) {{hl}}6. Degradation and Desertification: 32% of land affected by degradation and 25%{{/hl}} by desertification

Impacts of climate change

• Ocean Ecosystem
- Coral reefs decline {{hl}}70-90%{{/hl}} if warming above 1.5°C [[IPCC](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/)]
- Antarctica losing ice mass at an average rate of about {{hl}}150 billion{{/hl}} tons per year
- Greenland losing {{hl}}270 billion{{/hl}} tons per year, adding to sea level rise

• Economic losses
- Decline in labour productivity of up to {{hl}}40%{{/hl}}.
- {{hl}}3.8% of total{{/hl}} working hours could be lost by 2030 [[World Economic Forum](https://www.weforum.org/)]

• Agriculture
- ↓ kharif maize yields by 18 and {{hl}}23%{{/hl}} in 2050 and 2080 scenarios, respectively.
- For every degree of warming, {{hl}}10-25%{{/hl}} increase in crops lost to insect attacks.
- Exploitable fish biomass show ↓ >{{hl}}10%{{/hl}} by mid-century for many regions of world [[FAO](https://www.fao.org/faostat/)]

• Women
- {{hl}}158 million{{/hl}} more women and girls into poverty by 2050
- {{hl}}236 million{{/hl}} more women into hunger [[UN Women](https://www.unwomen.org/)]

• Extreme events
- Heatwave made {{hl}}45 times{{/hl}} more likely due to climate change
- {{hl}}14.83 crore{{/hl}} people in India will be living in severe climate hotspots by 2050 (Council on Energy, Environment and water)
- > {{hl}}80%{{/hl}} of Indian population lives in districts highly vulnerable to extreme weather events.

• Displacement
- India may face a migration of {{hl}}45 million{{/hl}} people by 2050.
- {{hl}}600 million{{/hl}} people could face food insecurity due to climate change- induced disruptions to agriculture and fisheries.
- Tuvalu expected to be one of the first countries to be completely lost to climate change.

Carbon Inequality
- Richest {{hl}}1%{{/hl}} responsible for more carbon emissions than the poorest {{hl}}66%{{/hl}}.
- Half of all emissions are due to {{hl}}1/10th{{/hl}} of the global population

IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report
- > {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} chance that global temperature rise will reach or surpass 1.5 degrees Celsius between 2021 and 2040.
- Per-capita GDP in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and West Asia remain lower than global average by 2050 [[IPCC 6th synthesis report](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/syr/)]

Climate finance

• Global
- **Global climate finance needs** are projected to exceed ${{hl}}10 trillion{{/hl}} annually by 2050 ([CAG](https://cag.gov.in/)).
- **Advanced economies** contributed {{hl}}45%{{/hl}} of climate finance, while **least** **developed countries (LDCs)** received only {{hl}}3% {{/hl}}- From 2018 to 2022 (GLCF 2024).
- **Adaptation funding gap:** Developing countries need ${{hl}}215–387 billion{{/hl}} annually, but receive just ${{hl}}28 billion in 2022{{/hl}} ([Adaptation Gap Report 2024](https://www.unep.org/resources/adaptation-gap-report-2024)).
- **Mitigation-adaptation imbalance**-> {{hl}}90%{{/hl}} of climate finance directed toward mitigation ([UNDP](https://hdr.undp.org/)).
- **Funding source:** > {{hl}}94%{{/hl}} of current climate investment comes through debt or equity, rather than grants (Climate Policy Initiative).

• India's Climate Finance Needs
- India estimates a ${{hl}}2.5 trillion{{/hl}} financing need by 2030 for its climate transition to achieve net-zero emissions by 2070.
- {{hl}}6–8 trillion USD{{/hl}} needed during 2015–2030 to transform current energy systems in India.
- **Adaptation spending:** ↑ from {{hl}}3.7% of GDP{{/hl}} in FY16 to {{hl}}5.6%{{/hl}} in FY22 ([Eco Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf))

• Quantified Goal on Climate Finance (NCQG) or Baku Finance Goal
- Triple finance to {{hl}}USD 300 billion{{/hl}} annually by 2035 (previous goal of {{hl}}USD 100 billion{{/hl}} annually).
- Secure efforts to mobilize ${{hl}}1.3 trillion{{/hl}} per year by 2035 from both public and private sources
- {{hl}}COP29{{/hl}}-> proposed climate finance goal of {{hl}}USD 300 billion{{/hl}} annually by 2035 is much lower than the estimated {{hl}}USD 5.1-6.8 trillion{{/hl}} needed by 2030 ([Eco Survey](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) {{hl}}11. LiFE: By 2030, LiFE could save consumers USD 440 billion globally.{{/hl}} {{hl}}12. Paris agreement status: Current pledges put world on track for a 2.5-2.9°C{{/hl}} temperature rise– far above the 1.5°C limit [[UNEP Emission Gap report](https://www.uncclearn.org/wp-content/uploads/library/EGR2025.pdf)]

India's Climate Commitments
• Panchamrit (COP-26)
- Non-fossil fuel energy capacity to 500 gigawatts (GW) by 2030;
- {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} of its energy needs from renewable sources by 2030;
- ↓ carbon emissions by {{hl}}1 billion tonnes{{/hl}} from the present until 2030;
- Reduce emissions intensity of its GDP by {{hl}}45%{{/hl}} by 2030.
- Net Zero emissions by 2070. **14. India’s demands: India wants to push developed nations to become carbon** negative rather than carbon neutral by 2050.

BIODIVERSITY

Protected areas
- 1014 Protected areas-> covers 1,75,169.42 km2 of geographical area -> ≈ {{hl}}5.32%{{/hl}}.
- {{hl}}72%{{/hl}} rise in the number and {{hl}}16%{{/hl}} growth in the total area from 2000 to 2023.
- Bid to double global protected areas affect India’s tribes
    - {{hl}}84%{{/hl}} of national parks are established in areas inhabited by STs.

Biodiversity hotspots
- India lost {{hl}}90% of area{{/hl}} under its four biodiversity hotspots (CSE Data, 2021)
- 25 species have gone extinct in these hotspots.
- **Global:** 36 biodiversity hotspots
    - Represent just {{hl}}2.5%{{/hl}} of Earth's land surface
    - Supports > half of the world's plant species as endemics
    - Supports {{hl}}43%{{/hl}} of bird, mammal, reptile and amphibian species as endemics.

Illegal wildlife trade
- {{hl}}4th most illegal trade{{/hl}} after arms, drugs and human trafficking.
- Annual value -> $7 - ${{hl}}23 billion {{/hl}}(2016 UN estimates)
- Rhino horn ({{hl}}29%{{/hl}}), followed by pangolin scales ({{hl}}28%{{/hl}}) and elephant ivory ({{hl}}15%{{/hl}}) [[World Wildlife Crime report, 2024](https://www.unodc.org/cofrb/uploads/documents/ECOS/World_Wildlife_Crime_Report_2024.pdf)] **4. Illegally traded plants: Cedars mahogany, holy wood, and Guiacum made up** biggest market at {{hl}}47%{{/hl}}.

Human wildlife conflict
- **Elephant deaths:** 94 elephants perished due to electrocution in 2023-24
- **Tiger deaths:** > 600 people were killed in tiger attacks in the country between 2014 and 2024, an average of 60 deaths annually
- **Agriculture loss:** Wild herbivores damage {{hl}}15-50%{{/hl}} of standing crops in field
- **Poaching:** > 6,900 poachers were arrested for killing and trafficking of 2,869 wildlife animals during the past {{hl}}10 years{{/hl}}
- India is among the top three countries globally for illegal wildlife trade via the airline sector.

Invasive species
• India
- India tops the list with 185 invasive alien plants in South Asia.
- {{hl}}66%{{/hl}} of country's natural systems threatened
- Economic cost could reach up to {{hl}}USD 182.6 billion.{{/hl}}
• Global
- 37,000 established alien species
- 1 in 10 species on IUCN Red List are threatened by invasive alien species.
- Annual economic costs exceed {{hl}}USD 423 billion.{{/hl}}

Coastal areas
- {{hl}}33.6%{{/hl}} of Indian coastline vulnerable to erosion, {{hl}}26.9%{{/hl}} was under accretion (growing) and {{hl}}39.6%{{/hl}} was in stable state.

Forests
• India State of Forest Report (2023)
- **Forest and Tree cover:** {{hl}}25.17 percent{{/hl}} of the geographical area and ({{hl}}21.76%{{/hl}} is forest cover and {{hl}}3.41%{{/hl}} is tree cover).
    - ↑ by 1,445.81 km², with a 156.41 km² rise in forest cover compared to 2021.
• State-wise data
- **Area wise** top three states having largest forest cover are Madhya Pradesh > Arunachal Pradesh > Chhattisgarh
- **Maximum increase (Forest and Tree Cover):** Chhattisgarh > Uttar Pradesh > Odisha > Rajasthan
- **Largest Decrease:** MP > Karnataka > Ladakh > Nagaland
- 19 states/UTs have above {{hl}}33 percent{{/hl}} of the geographical area under forest cover.
- **Mangrove cover**: {{hl}}4,992 sq km {{/hl}}- {{hl}}0.15%{{/hl}} of the total geographical area, with a net decrease of 7.43 km² since 2021.
- **Carbon stock:** {{hl}}30.43 billion tonnes{{/hl}} of CO2 equivalent.

Mangroves
- **Total mangrove cover:** {{hl}}4,992 sq km {{/hl}}([ISFR 2023](https://fsi.nic.in/uploads/isfr2023/isfr_book_eng-vol-1_2023.pdf))
- **Vulnerability**: By 2070, {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} of India’s mangroves will shift or vanish due to climate change [Birbal Sahni institute Palaeosciences]
- **Global:** Over {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} of world’s mangroves at risk of collapse, climate change leading factor; ([IUCN](https://www.iucn.org/)).

Coral reefs
• Global
- Cover less than {{hl}}1%{{/hl}} of ocean floor but most productive and diverse ecosystem.
- **Bleaching:** > {{hl}}60%{{/hl}} of world's coral reefs may have bleached in past year ([NOAA](https://www.noaa.gov/))
- **Effect of Climate change:** It **c**ould damage half of the world's reefs by 2035
- NOAA confirms {{hl}}4th global coral bleaching{{/hl}} event
• India
- **Bleaching:** {{hl}}84.6%{{/hl}} of coral reefs in Lakshadweep experienced bleaching during 2023-24 [Ministry of Earth Sciences informed (MoES)]
- It takes {{hl}}6-7 years{{/hl}} for Lakshadweep reefs to recover, without further disturbances
- Degradation can affect {{hl}}4.5 million{{/hl}} people in southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean.

Wetlands
- {{hl}}4.6% of land{{/hl}} as wetlands
- {{hl}}15.26 million hectares{{/hl}}
- India now has {{hl}}101 Ramsar sites{{/hl}} (covering {{hl}}13.88 lakh hectares{{/hl}} across 28 states/UTs as of August 2026, up from 89 sites earlier; highest in Asia) ([MoEFCC](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100) / [Ramsar Convention 2026](https://indianwetlands.in/wp-content/uploads/library/1761126102.pdf))
- **National Wetland Atlas (2011):** Gujarat ({{hl}}17.5%{{/hl}}), lowest in Mizoram ({{hl}}0.66%{{/hl}})
- India lost 2 out of 5 wetlands in last 3 decades
• Global
- {{hl}}35%{{/hl}} of the world's wetlands lost b/w 1970-2015
- {{hl}}30%{{/hl}} of coastal wetlands could be lost by 2100

Beaches
- {{hl}}18 Blue Flag Certified beaches{{/hl}} in India across 7 coastal states and 2 UTs as of the 2025-26 season (up from 12) ([MoEFCC Year-End Review 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100))
- {{hl}}89%{{/hl}} of shoreline of A&N islands eroded by Bay of Bengal
- {{hl}}33.6%{{/hl}} of Indian coastline was vulnerable to erosion

Species
- **Extinct species:** Indian Cheetah, pink-headed duck, and the Great Indian Bustard due to desertification.

• Tiger
- ↑ by {{hl}}30%{{/hl}} in the last {{hl}}20 years{{/hl}}.
- 3,682 tigers (range 3,167–3,925, accounting for ~{{hl}}75% of global{{/hl}} wild tiger population) ([NTCA All India Tiger Estimation 2022/2023](https://ntca.gov.in/tiger-reserves/))
    - {{hl}}53.2%{{/hl}} of tiger deaths occurred within Tiger Reserves
    - {{hl}}35.22%{{/hl}} happened outside boundary of TRs ([NTCA](https://ntca.gov.in/tiger-reserves/))
    - Tiger deaths in 2023 is highest (178) since 2012.

• Elephants
- India has the largest number of wild Asian Elephants
- Decline in India's Elephant Population-> From 19.8K in 2017 to 15.9K in 2023 ([WII](https://wii.gov.in/))
- 29,964 elephants (2017 census by Project Elephant).
- {{hl}}60%{{/hl}} of the species’ global population in India.

• Birds Population
• State of India’s Birds (2023)
- {{hl}}60%{{/hl}} of bird species declined in India over a period of {{hl}}30 years{{/hl}}
- {{hl}}29%{{/hl}} are stable, and {{hl}}11%{{/hl}} have shown increases.
• Global
- {{hl}}48%{{/hl}} of 11,000 surviving bird species experiencing decline
- {{hl}}13.5%{{/hl}} of bird species face risk of global extinction, with 798 species classified as vulnerable, 460 as endangered, and 223 as critically endangered. **14. Ecosystem services: Total value of global ecosystem services for one year is b/w** 16 to {{hl}}54 trillion USD{{/hl}}

ENERGY - RENEWABLE & NON-RENEWABLE
- India’s Energy Mix (Sources and Shares) [ As per [Energy Statistics India 2025](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports) , [MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1767781372753_1380ce82-f5a5-440d-99e6-e6b35af0deb5_GDP_Press_Note_on_FAE_2025-26.pdf)]

Non-renewable energy

• Coal energy

- **Consumption:** {{hl}}164.3 million{{/hl}} metric standard cubic meters per day (mmscmd).
- CNG vehicle sales jump {{hl}}38%{{/hl}} in FY2024

• Nuclear energy
- {{hl}}5th largest source{{/hl}} of electricity
- {{hl}}4%{{/hl}} of the total electricity generation
- 25 operable nuclear energy reactors with a total installed capacity of {{hl}}8.88 GW{{/hl}}
- **Target:** {{hl}}1 lakh MW by 2047{{/hl}}

Renewable energy

• Solar energy
- **Potential:** {{hl}}748 GWp {{/hl}}(National Institute of Solar Energy)
- **Installed capacity:** {{hl}}150.26 GW as of 31 March 2026{{/hl}} (including {{hl}}110.43 GW{{/hl}} utility-scale, {{hl}}25.73 GW{{/hl}} rooftop solar, and {{hl}}14.10 GW{{/hl}} PM-KUSUM/off-grid; up from {{hl}}100.33 GW{{/hl}} in Jan 2025 after a record {{hl}}44.61 GW{{/hl}} addition in FY26) ([MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
    - **Capacity increase:** {{hl}}2.82 GW in 2014{{/hl}} to {{hl}}100GW in 2025{{/hl}}.
    - Utility scale installation: {{hl}}18.5 GW{{/hl}}
• Rooftop solar (RTS)
- **Market:** Surged from {{hl}}2.5 GW in FY21{{/hl}} to {{hl}}25.73 GW cumulative rooftop solar capacity as of March 2026{{/hl}} (with {{hl}}8.71 GW{{/hl}} added in FY26 alone) ([MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
    - **Capacity addition**: India added {{hl}}1.2 GW{{/hl}} of rooftop solar capacity in the first quarter (Q1) of 2025, up {{hl}}232%{{/hl}} year-over-year from {{hl}}366.5 MW{{/hl}}
- **Households:** Over {{hl}}42 lakh households{{/hl}} benefited from rooftop solar installations till March 2026 (with PM Surya Ghar touching {{hl}}18.71 lakh{{/hl}} installations / {{hl}}22.7 lakh{{/hl}} households in FY26, up from {{hl}}8.51 lakh{{/hl}} installations in FY25) ([MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039))
    - **New Solar Power Scheme:** Electrifies 100,000 households in tribal areas, providing off-grid solar systems for 63,000 villages, 1,500 multi-purpose centers, and 2,000 public institutions under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan.
    - **PM-Surya Ghar Yojana:** Aims for rooftop solar installations in {{hl}}10 million{{/hl}} households, targeting {{hl}}40-45 GW{{/hl}} capacity by 2027.
• World position
- {{hl}}3rd largest solar power{{/hl}} producer
- {{hl}}5th{{/hl}} in solar PV deployment

• Wind energy
- **Potential:** {{hl}}695.5 GW{{/hl}} at 120 meters and {{hl}}1,164 GW{{/hl}} at 150 meters above ground level
- **Target:** {{hl}}500 GW{{/hl}} renewable energy by 2030
- {{hl}}140 GW{{/hl}} from wind power.
- **Installed capacity:** {{hl}}56.09 GW as of 31 March 2026{{/hl}} (up from {{hl}}50.04 GW{{/hl}} in April 2025, with a record annual addition of {{hl}}6.05 GW in FY26{{/hl}}) [[MNRE 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)]
    - **Potential states:** Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

content_markdown:
POLLUTION & WASTE MANAGEMENT

Plastic pollution

• India
- **Annual:** Generates {{hl}}9.3 million tonnes{{/hl}} of plastic pollution annually.
- **Daily:** {{hl}}26,000 tonnes{{/hl}} of plastic waste – every day -> equivalent of 26,000 small cars!
- **Per capita plasti**c waste production ({{hl}}8 kg{{/hl}} per year)
- **Plastic recycling:** Just {{hl}}8%{{/hl}}
- **Single use plastic waste:** India ranked {{hl}}3rd globally{{/hl}}; contributes to {{hl}}5.5 million tonnes{{/hl}} per year.

• Global
- **Waste generation:** {{hl}}268 million tonnes in 2022{{/hl}}.
- **Largest consumers:** China ({{hl}}20%{{/hl}}), US ({{hl}}18%{{/hl}}), EU ({{hl}}16%{{/hl}}), India ({{hl}}6%{{/hl}}) and Japan ({{hl}}4%{{/hl}})
- **Per capita consumption** ->highest in the US at {{hl}}216 kg{{/hl}} per person, Japan ({{hl}}129 kg{{/hl}} per person) and EU ({{hl}}87 kg{{/hl}} per person).

Air pollution

• World Air Quality Report (2024 & 2025 - IQAir)
- **Rank:** India ranked {{hl}}6th most polluted country{{/hl}} (out of 143) in the 2025 World Air Quality Report [was {{hl}}5th{{/hl}} in 2024 and {{hl}}3rd{{/hl}} in 2023] ([IQAir 2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries))
- **PM2.5 Reduction:** National average PM2.5 concentration declined further to {{hl}}48.9 µg/m³ in 2025{{/hl}}, down from {{hl}}50.6 µg/m³ in 2024{{/hl}} and {{hl}}54.4 µg/m³ in 2023{{/hl}} ([IQAir 2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries)).
    - **WHO safe limi**t: {{hl}}5 µg/m³{{/hl}}.
- **Delhi & Indian Cities ->** New Delhi remained the **most polluted capital city in the world** for the {{hl}}8th consecutive year{{/hl}} ({{hl}}91.8 µg/m³ in 2024{{/hl}})
- Loni (UP) was the most polluted city in 2025 at {{hl}}112.5 µg/m³{{/hl}}, and {{hl}}66 of the world's 100 most polluted cities{{/hl}} (and 13 of top 20 in 2024) are in India ([IQAir 2025/2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries)).
    - {{hl}}13 of the 20 most polluted cities{{/hl}} in the world are in India.
- **Global (2025 Report):** Top 5 most polluted countries -> Pakistan ({{hl}}67.3 µg/m³{{/hl}}), Bangladesh ({{hl}}66.1 µg/m³{{/hl}}), Tajikistan ({{hl}}57.3 µg/m³{{/hl}}), Chad ({{hl}}53.6 µg/m³{{/hl}}), and DR Congo ({{hl}}50.2 µg/m³{{/hl}}) [in 2024: Chad ({{hl}}91.8 µg/m³{{/hl}}), Bangladesh ({{hl}}78 µg/m³{{/hl}}), Pakistan ({{hl}}73.7 µg/m³{{/hl}}), Congo ({{hl}}58.2 µg/m³{{/hl}})] ([IQAir 2025/2026](https://www.iqair.com/world-most-polluted-countries)).

Mercury pollution
- **India-** {{hl}}2nd largest mercury emitter{{/hl}} -> {{hl}}144.7 tonnes{{/hl}} Hg/year
- India imports over 250 metric tonnes of mercury each year
- India leaks > {{hl}}220 tonnes{{/hl}} into the environment from known sources (Toxics Link, a NGO)
- > {{hl}}70%{{/hl}} to {{hl}}80%{{/hl}} of India's mercury emissions due to coal usage.

• Global position
- Current levels in the atmosphere are up to {{hl}}500 %{{/hl}} above natural levels.
- **In Oceans:** {{hl}}200 %{{/hl}} above natural levels. {{hl}}4. Land pollution: 33% of the country’s total geographic area —are affected by soil{{/hl}} degradation, salinity, and vegetation loss.

Noise pollution
• Optimum noise level ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535))
- 45 dB during the day and 35 dB at night.
- Anything above 80 dB is hazardous.
- 12,000 premature deaths and 48,000 new cases of ischaemic heart disease every year (European Environment agency)
- Noise level of >80 decibels for more than 8 hours a day increases changes in breathing patterns ([WHO](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240091535))

Light pollution
- Artificial light increasing by around {{hl}}2%{{/hl}} per year globally.

Biomedical waste
- India generates {{hl}}743 tonnes{{/hl}} of biomedical waste daily and about {{hl}}640 tonnes{{/hl}} is treated ([CPCB report](https://cpcb.nic.in/))

Waste to Energy conversion
- **Total waste:** {{hl}}65 million tonnes{{/hl}} of waste every year;
    - estimated to go up to {{hl}}165 million tonnes by 2030{{/hl}} and {{hl}}436 million tonnes by 2050{{/hl}}
• Conversion Potential
- {{hl}}1700 MW{{/hl}} from urban waste (1500 from MSW and {{hl}}225 MW{{/hl}} from sewage) and about {{hl}}1300 MW{{/hl}} from industrial waste [[Ministry of New and Renewable Energy](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)]
- **Current status:** {{hl}}75%{{/hl}} of municipal waste gets collected; only 22 to {{hl}}28 percent{{/hl}} is processed
- 12 operational and eight non-operational waste-to-energy plants in India in 10 states as of November 2022.

Solid waste management
- India generated {{hl}}170,000 tonnes{{/hl}} of municipal solid waste per day
    - **Collection and treatment:** About {{hl}}156,000 tonnes{{/hl}} were collected, of which nearly {{hl}}54 per cent{{/hl}} was treated, and
    - **Deposition in landfills:** {{hl}}24%{{/hl}} was deposited in landfills ([CPCB 2024](https://cpcb.nic.in/)).
• Type of waste
- {{hl}}50-55%{{/hl}} of waste in Indian cities is biodegradable wet waste;
- {{hl}}35%{{/hl}} is non-biodegradable wet waste
- {{hl}}10%{{/hl}} is inert.
- **Per capita waste generation** -> B/w 0.2 Kg to 0.6 Kg per day in cities with population ranging from {{hl}}1.0 lakh{{/hl}} to {{hl}}50 lakhs.{{/hl}}
- **Projections**: Indian cities will generate approximately {{hl}}435 million tonnes{{/hl}} of solid waste by 2050 ([MoHUA](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526) 2021).

E-Waste

• India
- {{hl}}3rd biggest e-waste generator{{/hl}} behind China and the U.S.
- {{hl}}67%{{/hl}} of India's e-waste remains unprocessed ([Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2210100))

• Global [Global E-waste Monitor 2024 Report]
- Increase in global e-waste generation, rising from {{hl}}34 billion {{/hl}}(bn) kg in 2010 to {{hl}}62 bn kg in 2022{{/hl}}.
- Of this {{hl}}62 bn kg{{/hl}}, only {{hl}}13.8 bn kg{{/hl}} is documented as ‘formally collected and recycled in an environmentally sound manner’.
- {{hl}}62 million{{/hl}} tons of “e-waste” was generated in 2022-> enough to fill tractor-trailers that could be lined up bumper to bumper around globe.

Circular economy
- **India:** India's circular economy could touch ${{hl}}45 billion by 2030{{/hl}}.
- **Global:** Transition to a circular economy could generate ${{hl}}4.5 trillion{{/hl}} in additional economic output globally by 2030.

WATER & ITS CONSERVATION

Water Scarcity
- **Water Scarcity**: As per World Bank, Annual per-capita water availability
    - < 1700 m³: Water Stressed condition
    - < 1000 m³: Water Scarcity condition (India =: Around 1500 m³ (CWC))
- **Global Scenario**: Water scarcity affects more than {{hl}}40%{{/hl}} of the global population
• India’s Scenario
- {{hl}}18%{{/hl}} of world population lives in India but it has just {{hl}}4%{{/hl}} of world’s water resources.
- India is the second-largest consumer of water, using {{hl}}20.1 per cent{{/hl}} of global water resources.
- It ranks {{hl}}133rd{{/hl}} in water availability per capita
- **Per Capita Use (India):** Average annual per capita water availability for the year 2021 was 1,486 cubic meters ([Ministry of Jal Shakti](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2220203®=3&lang=1))
- **Projected water demand**: Per capita water use is projected to increase from 85 litres per capita per day (lpcd) in 2000 to 125 lpcd by 2025 and 170 lpcd by 2050.
- **Access**: {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} has no access to safe water.
- **Deaths**: Around 2 Lac/year (due to lack of access to safe water)
- **Economic Burden**: Loss of {{hl}}6% of GDP{{/hl}}

Water Pollution
- **Surface Water Pollution**: {{hl}}80%{{/hl}} of surface water is polluted
- **Pollution Levels**: {{hl}}70%{{/hl}} water resources are polluted ([Composite Water Management Index](https://www.niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-03/Composite-Water-Management-Index.pdf))
- **Source of River Pollution**:
    - {{hl}}80%{{/hl}} of river pollution -> untreated waste
    - {{hl}}20%{{/hl}} of river pollution -> Industries

Groundwater Crisis
- India is the largest groundwater user globally ({{hl}}26%{{/hl}} of world).
- **Annual groundwater extraction:** {{hl}}247.22 BCM in 2025{{/hl}} (245.64 BCM in 2024; 241.34 BCM in 2023), out of 407.75 BCM annual extractable groundwater resources ([CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resource Assessment 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf)).
- The country's {{hl}}Stage of Ground Water Extraction (SoE) is 60.63% in 2025{{/hl}} ({{hl}}60.47%{{/hl}} in 2024; {{hl}}59.26%{{/hl}} in 2023) ([CGWB 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf)).
- India consumes more groundwater than the US and China combined
- Annual groundwater recharge -> {{hl}}448.52 BCM in 2025{{/hl}} (up from 446.90 BCM in 2024 and 432 BCM in 2017) ([Ministry of Jal Shakti](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2220203®=3&lang=1) / [CGWB 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf))
- Ground Water Table -> 0.3 ↓/Year
• Dependency
- {{hl}}62%{{/hl}} of irrigation needs are met through groundwater.
- {{hl}}85%{{/hl}} of rural and {{hl}}50%{{/hl}} of urban water supply depend on groundwater.
- {{hl}}10.8% of groundwater assessment units (730 out of 6,762 units) are over-exploited in 2025{{/hl}} (down from {{hl}}17.2%{{/hl}} in 2017), while {{hl}}73.14% (4,946 units) are in the Safe category{{/hl}} (up from {{hl}}62.6%{{/hl}} in 2017) ([CGWB 2025](https://cgwb.gov.in/GWRA/GWRA_2025.pdf))
    - GW depletion rate could triple by 2080, if Indian farmers continued to draw groundwater at the current rate.
• Annual Groundwater Quality Report 2024
- Largest user of groundwater
- Largest area under groundwater irrigation in the world.
• Uses
- {{hl}}87%{{/hl}} of extracted groundwater in agriculture and {{hl}}11%{{/hl}} is used for domestic purposes.

Ocean pollution
- As of 2025, 75 to {{hl}}199 million tonnes{{/hl}} of plastic and waste in our oceans.
- {{hl}}171 trillion{{/hl}} pieces of plastic estimated to be floating in the world's oceans.

Oil pollution
- Ten oil spills of more than seven tonnes were recorded from tanker incidents in 2024

Urban water crisis
- {{hl}}48%{{/hl}} of India’s urban water supply comes from groundwater (CSE)
- {{hl}}40%{{/hl}} of people in urban areas in India don't get tap water [[National Sample Survey Office](https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports)]
- By 2030 India’s water demand would be double due to rapid urbanization and little infra planning (UN report)

subject: HISTORY
content_markdown:
BRITISH COLONIAL ECONOMY

• Economic drain by British
- **Scholars**:
    - **Romesh Chandra Dutt**: In early {{hl}}20th century{{/hl}} ≈ £{{hl}}20 million{{/hl}} flew out of India.
    - **MG Ranade**: In his book "Essay on Indian Economics," he claimed that Britishers drained more than one-third of India's wealth into England.
    - **Dadabhai Naoroji**: India's tax burden in 1886 was {{hl}}14.3% of total{{/hl}} revenue, significantly higher than England's {{hl}}6.93%{{/hl}}.
    - **Angus Maddison** (British economist): India's share of the world income went from {{hl}}27%{{/hl}} in 1700 AD (compared to Europe's share of {{hl}}23%{{/hl}}) to {{hl}}3%{{/hl}} in 1950.
- **Reports**:
    - {{hl}}'Takers Not Makers: The Unjust Poverty and Unearned Wealth of Colonial Inheritance' report, 2025 ({{/hl}}[Oxfam](https://www.oxfam.org/en/research/takers-not-makers-unjust-poverty-and-unearned-wealth-colonialism)):
        - Wealth Drain during Colonial Period -> Between 1765 and 1900, UK drained ${{hl}}64.82 trillion{{/hl}} from India, with ${{hl}}33.8 trillion{{/hl}} going to the top {{hl}}10%{{/hl}}.
- **India and its Contradictions**: In the {{hl}}18th century{{/hl}}, India became a land of contrasts because extreme poverty and extreme luxury existed side by side.

• Famines
- Between 1730 to 1947 🢥 31 famines, loss of life of {{hl}}8.5 cr.{{/hl}} Indians
- In 1770, there was a terrible Famine in Bengal which killed about 1 Crore people.

• Land Revenue systems
- **Permanent Settlement**:
    - Covered {{hl}}20%{{/hl}} of British India
    - The state received 10/{{hl}}11th{{/hl}} of the rent the zamindars received from the peasantry, with only 1/{{hl}}11th going to the{{/hl}} zamindars themselves.
    - Between 1794 and 1819, {{hl}}68%{{/hl}} of zamindari land was sold in Bengal.
- **Ryotwari System**:
    - Covered {{hl}}51%{{/hl}} area of British India.
    - Revenue was fixed at very high rate ({{hl}}45-50%{{/hl}})

• State of Industry
- Up until 1750, India produced about {{hl}}25%{{/hl}} of the world's industrial output.
- India had a {{hl}}25%{{/hl}} share of the global textile trade in the early {{hl}}18th{{/hl}} century.
- By 1664, the English East India Company imported more than 750,000 pieces of cotton goods from India, which accounted for {{hl}}73 per cent{{/hl}} of the Company’s total trade.

• Infrastructure
- On April 16, 1853 -> first railway line in India spanning upto 34 kilometers between Boribandar (Bombay) to Thane.
- Built {{hl}}6000 kms{{/hl}} of track by 1869 and {{hl}}45,000 km{{/hl}} of track by 1905 with the help of private enterprises.
- **Railway length** = ~69,439 route km (~{{hl}}1.32 lakh{{/hl}} track km) today ([Economic Survey 2025-26](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey/doc/echapter.pdf)) --> ~{{hl}}53,000–54,000 km{{/hl}} built during British rule before 1947 ([Ministry of Railways](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298526)).
